newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Syria interested in fresh talks with Israel -envoy.
newsitem.headline: Syria interested in fresh talks with Israel -envoy.

text.p: Syria has expressed interest in resuming stalled peace talks with Israel, Norway's foreign minister told Israel's foreign minister on Wednesday.

Bjorn Godal brought the message to Israel's David Levy in Jerusalem after visiting Syria. Israel froze five-year-old negotiations with Syria after a series of Islamic bombings in the Jewish state over a year ago.
"I was reassured by the Syrian president and foreign minister that they take interest in the furthering of the peace process," Godal told reporters after a meeting with Levy.
"They expressed positive interest on the revival of the Syria-Lebanon track...and this was the message that they wanted to convey to me."
Syria wants Israel to withdraw from the Golan Heights, a strategic plateau it captured in the 1967 Middle East War.

Israel's previous Labour government indicated it would make concessions on the Heights. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government, in office far nearly a year, insists on maintaining Israeli control of the Golan.
"If Syria wants peace it must talk to Israel," he said. "I say again, I am ready to meet the foreign minister of Syria anywhere, any time...to clarify the possibility of going back to talks."
